newsitem.title: USA: Chrysalis says sees Q4 charges, loss.
newsitem.headline: Chrysalis says sees Q4 charges, loss.

text.p: Chrysalis International Corp said Thursday that, without taking into account certain charges, it anticipates that earnings for the fourth quarter of 1996 will be below management's expectations and will result in a loss.

It said the charges of about $3.6 million are related to its acquisition of a clinical drug development business on December 18. The charges will be reflected in the fourth quarter results and include merger-related costs, the name change to Chrysalis from DNX Corp and other related items.

The company also announced that an international pharmaceutical concern that has an existing relationship with it has awarded the company a new, multinational clinical trial for Phase II and III drug development services, which it said may exceed $20 million in revenues.

"While we were disappointed with some aspects of our fourth quarter results, nevertheless, the formation of Chrysalis has already resulted in new opportunities whereby the company is being considered for larger preclinical as well as clinical studies," said Paul J. Schmitt, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Chrysalis.
The company explained that during the fourth quarter, results from the preclinical business were consistent with management expectations.

However, it noted that revenues in the recently acquired BioClin Group were negatively affected in the fourth quarter because management focused on completing the merger with BioClin, and by long lead times in converting proposals into revenues. The merger was completed December 19.

"While the efforts and costs expended to properly present Chrysalis to our global client base and expand the preclinical and clinical businesses will continue to impact results for the first half of 1997, the formation of Chrysalis is already yielding opportunities to participate in new and larger drug development programs with our clients." Schmitt noted.."

Following completion of the merger, Chrysalis said it retired about $9.0 million of outstanding debt of the acquired business and established a new $3.0 million working capital line of credit for European operations.

In a separate statement, Chrysalis announced it had hired Sheldon Brookman as vice president and general manager for its North American clinical business. Brookman was recently vice president, clinical operations of PPD-Pharmaco and was previously, executive director, clinical research operations at Sandoz Pharmaceutical Corp.

Chrysalis is a global provider of drug development services. The company offers preclinical and clinical services necessary to develop drugs emerging from research through to regulatory approval and market introduction.
